$comment: Read from Google's own discovery document: users.messages.send -> POST gmail/v1/users/{userId}/messages/send, request Message, response Message.
title: Gmail message
description: Send an email from a connected Gmail account.
$idempotencyComment: Gmail offers no idempotency key on messages.send -- the discovery document has neither a header nor a parameter for one. So this is honestly unsafe-to-replay with no way to make it safe: a retried durable run sends a SECOND email, to a real person, which is the least recallable side effect in the estate so far.

compose.$comment: Gmail's Message.raw, quoted from the discovery document: 'The entire email message in an RFC 2822 formatted and base64url encoded string.' Not to/subject/body -- ONE opaque string containing a whole email. Nobody hand-writes RFC 2822, so the composition happens in the generated code and the parity suite proves all three runtimes produce the same bytes.

config.label: Send as
config.description: Whose mailbox to send from. `me` is the connected account and is almost always what you want.
config.$comment: In the PATH. `me` is a literal Gmail understands, which is why it is the default rather than an address -- an address here has to be one the connected account is allowed to send as, and getting that wrong is a 403 that reads like an auth problem.

config.label: To
config.description: Recipient address. Several can be given, comma separated, exactly as an email client accepts them.

config.label: Cc
config.description: Copied recipients, comma separated. Left empty the header is omitted entirely rather than sent blank.

config.label: Message
config.description: The plain-text body. It is sent as text/plain; UTF-8, so accented characters and emoji survive.

outputShape.description: Gmail's id for the sent message.
The thread it landed in. Gmail groups by subject and references, so a reply to an existing conversation shares this.
